item.title: Judge approves $7.25bn settlement for Roundup weedkiller cancer claims
item.description:

item.title: Russian missiles hit Poland: What happened, and could NATO respond?
item.description:
Three Russian projectiles came down in Poland on Friday, prompting NATO to condemn what it called a grave violation of Polish airspace. A suspected jet-powered drone and a missile struck separate locations near the Ukrainian border, while another missile crashed just 35 kilometres from an area where European troops are taking part in military exercises. Meanwhile, troops from eight NATO countries are conducting drills in neighbouring Lithuania. With US-led peace talks yet to make a breakthrough, tensions between Europe and Russia remain high. Peter O’Brien reports.

item.title: Bessent says no further restrictions are needed for Nvidia chip exports to China
item.description:
Scrutiny of the broader US semiconductor sector intensified amid growing hawkishness in Washington sparked by the controversy surrounding chip giant Nvidia’s sales to China. Since 2022, the US has fitfully sought to curtail Chinese access to cutting-edge chip technology, but that effort has been catalyzed in recent days by an espionage scandal that led to the ousting of Nvidia’s CEO. California officials are now investigating whether the company misled investors about its links to Beijing , while federal lawmakers released files showing the US approved sales of nearly 880,000 chips to China — including to firms seen as fronts for the Chinese military ; Caixin reported China’s tech giants were “ reeling ” from the prospect of sudden, new semiconductor restrictions. — Prashant Rao

item.title: EU and Indonesia sign trade deal
item.description:
London and Brussels are poised to sign a deal aimed at resetting relations still blighted by the UK’s vote to exit the EU a decade ago. The limited agreement would allow increased food and drinks trade, a re-linking of their carbon markets, and closer migration cooperation. But the details mask a potentially grander ambition: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said he hopes Britain will rejoin the bloc in his lifetime , and the country is seeing a revived debate on the benefits and costs of membership . Brussels would probably be welcoming, but equally is unwilling to make major concessions. “We didn’t want them to leave,” one European diplomat told Politico. “ They broke up with us. Now we are over them .” — Prashant Rao

item.title: Senate permitting bill speeds up renewables, divides greens over oil and gas
item.description:
The Senate passed a sweeping, bipartisan bill Thursday night that's designed to cut permitting timelines for energy and infrastructure projects. Why it matters: The eyes of the entire energy industry are on this bill. If it becomes law, it could transform how America builds energy infrastructure, with major implications for everything from electricity costs to data centers. Getting rid of bureaucratic hurdles and creating a more predictable process for energy projects is a top priority for the fossil fuels and renewables sectors. But critics argue the plan, which has White House support, would unacceptably weaken environmental protections and the rights of Native American tribes. Driving the news: The vote was 62-33. The bill would still have to pass the House before the end of the year, and any differences would have to be worked out by both chambers before President Trump could sign…

item.title: Brooks and Capehart on Trump's summit with Putin and Xi
item.description:
China's Xi Jinping places himself firmly in the center of the trilateral summit with Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump. Doug Mills/Getty Images It was touted as a history-making summit of the year. Presidents Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping sat down on Nov. 19, 2026, in Shenzhen, China, on the sideline of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit , for the first such trilateral meeting of the three leaders. Going into the talks, the trio had much to dicuss: the ongoing war in Ukraine , Middle East conflict and the march of artificial intelligence technology chief among them. But what did 90 minutes of conversation deliver? As an expert on U.S.-China relations at Harvard Kennedy School , I saw a lot of style, but less substance.
